result:
Compiles cleanly (`mvn -o compile`).

Two places constrained the key length, both now 128:

- **`src/main/resources/db/migration/V2__widen_idempotency_key.sql`** (new) — `ALTER TABLE payment ALTER COLUMN idempotency_key SET DATA TYPE VARCHAR(128)`. I added a new versioned migration rather than editing `V1__init.sql:3` in place, since a migration that has already been applied elsewhere shouldn't change its checksum. If this schema has never been deployed, say so and I'll fold the change into V1 instead.
- **`src/main/java/mn/pay/Payment.java:14`** — `@Column(nullable = false, length = 128)`. This was implicitly 255 (the JPA default), so Hibernate-generated DDL and validation disagreed with the 64-char column; it now matches the table.

Nothing else caps the length: `PaymentValidator.check` only rejects null/blank, the GraphQL `String!` argument is unbounded, and `PaymentDto` doesn't carry the key. `SET DATA TYPE` is standard SQL and works on Postgres and H2; if your target is MySQL it needs `MODIFY idempotency_key VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL` — I couldn't tell which engine you use, as the repo has no datasource config or Flyway dependency.
